label: an approximate reconstruction from the cited claims, not the experiment's geometry

quantities.name: depth_x0
quantities.definition: x/X0 along the crystal axis, front-face centre to rear-face centre
quantities.derivation: 230 mm (detector-atlas:C125) x 8.28 g/cm3 (detector-atlas:C130) / 7.39 g/cm2 (PDG); CMS states 25.8 X0 (detector-atlas:C125)

sources.source: PDG Atomic and Nuclear Properties, lead tungstate (2025 web edition)
sources.value: radiation length 7.39 g/cm2 (0.8903 cm at 8.300 g/cm3)
sources.method: Tsai's formula with Bragg addition over mass fractions (RPP 2024 section 34.4.2)

independence.result: independent of Geant4: the crystal length is CMS's design value and the radiation length PDG's tabulation; CMS's own 25.8 X0 is 230 mm / 8.9 mm from PDG 2004, not a simulation output. The reference is not a Geant4 output. Geant4 computes radiation lengths with the same Tsai formula, so agreement validates the geometry and the material definition (composition and density), not Geant4's radiation-length physics.

approximations: one barrel crystal as a symmetric trd, 22 x 22 to 26 x 26 mm2 nominal; the true crystals are 17 shape pairs varying with eta
PbWO4 by stoichiometric mass fractions with CMS's density 8.28 g/cm3 (PDG gives 8.300, 0.24% more)
the crystal in vacuum at the origin: its placement in the barrel (radius 1.29 m, 3 degree tilt) is not modelled, and does not enter the quantity
status: validated-in-scope (comparison with cited values, not confirmation)
